questions.question: Define the term 'GNI per head'.
questions.correctAnswer: GNI per head is the total value of goods and services produced by a country plus net income from abroad, divided by the total population, measured in US dollars.

questions.question: Describe two limitations of using GNI per head as a measure of development.
questions.correctAnswer: First, GNI per head hides inequality within a country - wealth may be concentrated among a small elite while the majority live in poverty. Second, it does not account for the informal economy (e.g. subsistence farming or street trading) which is significant in many LICs and NEEs.

questions.question: Explain why the HDI is considered a better measure of development than GNI alone.
questions.correctAnswer: The HDI is a composite measure that combines economic (GNI per head), health (life expectancy), and education (mean years of schooling) indicators. This gives a more complete picture of development than GNI alone, which only measures economic wealth. For example, Equatorial Guinea has relatively high GNI from oil but low HDI because wealth doesn't translate into better health or education for most

questions.question: Outline the key characteristics of Stage 3 of the Demographic Transition Model.
questions.correctAnswer: In Stage 3, birth rates begin to fall while death rates remain low. This is due to increased access to contraception, better education (especially for women), urbanisation, and lower infant mortality. The population continues to grow but at a slowing rate.

questions.question: Suggest reasons why death rates fall before birth rates as a country develops.
questions.correctAnswer: Death rates fall first because improvements in healthcare, sanitation, and food supply have an immediate impact on mortality. Birth rates remain high initially due to cultural norms, lack of contraception access, and because high infant mortality encourages families to have more children. It takes time for social attitudes and access to family planning to change.

questions.question: Compare the development indicators you would expect to find in an LIC and a HIC.
questions.correctAnswer: In an LIC you would expect: high birth rate (30-45), high infant mortality (40-80 per 1,000), low life expectancy (50-60 years), low literacy rate (40-70%), and low GNI per head (below $1,045). In a HIC you would expect: low birth rate (8-12), low infant mortality (2-5 per 1,000), high life expectancy (78-84 years), high literacy rate (99%+), and high GNI per head (above $12,746).
